batchName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476) - Medium Batch 1
chapterName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476)

questions.question: What idea, shared by pagans and Christians alike, did the author of The City of God reject?
options: That true religion should bring worldly success
That the end of the world was far off
That Rome had been founded by the gods
That barbarians could never be Christians
That emperors should be worshipped
questions.explanation: The bishop rejected the idea that true religion guarantees worldly success. He argued Christians' real home was a heavenly city no earthly disaster could touch.
questions.sourceQuote: He rejected the idea, shared by pagans and Christians alike, that true religion should bring worldly success.

questions.question: The general who crowned his son Romulus Augustus in 475 had once served as what?
options: The pope's treasurer
Odoacer's tutor
Attila's secretary
Alaric's envoy
A Vandal admiral
questions.explanation: The boy's father had once been Attila's secretary. He was later killed by his rebellious mercenaries after breaking a promise of land.
questions.sourceQuote: In 475 Orestes, a general who had once been Attila's secretary, drove out the reigning emperor and crowned his own young son.

questions.question: To help raise the huge ransom Alaric demanded in 408, what did the Romans melt down?
options: Imperial coins of the East
Legionary armour
Pagan statues
Bronze church bells
The doors of the Senate house
questions.explanation: Pagan statues were melted to complete the payment. The city paid about 5,000 pounds of gold and 30,000 pounds of silver.
questions.sourceQuote: Pagan statues were melted down to make up the sum.

questions.question: What advantage helped the Eastern Empire survive weaknesses that also affected the West?
options: No barbarian soldiers in its army
Freedom from plague and climate change
A lasting alliance with the Huns
A far larger and richer Senate
Geography: Constantinople's walls and the sea
questions.explanation: Walls and sea protected the eastern heartland. The West, by contrast, had some 2,000 km of Rhine and Danube frontier to guard.
questions.sourceQuote: Its advantage was geography: Constantinople's walls and the sea shielded its heartland, while the West had some 2,000 km of Rhine and Danube frontier to guard.

questions.question: What were Alaric's real demands during his sieges of Rome?
options: Land and grain for his people
The return of all Gothic slaves
Control of the city of Constantinople
The hand of the emperor's sister
The throne of the Western Empire
questions.explanation: Alaric mainly wanted land and grain for his people. The emperor in Ravenna refused even that and answered with insults.
questions.sourceQuote: Alaric's real demands were modest: land and grain for his people.

questions.question: What puzzling thing did the West's half-Vandal commander-in-chief do in Greece?
options: He sold the Goths grain at a profit
He twice cornered Alaric and twice let him escape
He refused to fight and resigned his command
He made Alaric his heir and son-in-law
He handed Greece over to the Huns
questions.explanation: He cornered Alaric twice and let him go both times, and historians still argue why. He later fought Alaric in Italy at Pollentia and Verona.
questions.sourceQuote: Twice he cornered Alaric in Greece and twice let him escape, and historians still argue why.

questions.question: One modern scholar has counted how many different theories for the fall of the Western Empire?
questions.explanation: A scholar counted 210 theories. Today historians point to plague, climate, migration, civil wars, crushing taxes and an elite unwilling to pay for defence.
questions.sourceQuote: One modern scholar has counted 210 different theories.

questions.question: What excuse did Attila use to invade the West in 451?
options: Rome sheltering his rebellious nephew
A claim to the eastern emperor's throne
Unpaid wages for his mercenaries
Revenge for the murder of a Hunnic envoy
A claim to the emperor's sister and half the West
questions.explanation: The emperor's sister, trapped in an engagement she hated, sent Attila her ring and a plea for help. He claimed her as his bride, with half the western empire as dowry.
questions.sourceQuote: Attila claimed her as his bride, with half the western empire as her dowry, and in 451 crossed the Rhine.

questions.question: What happened at the Battle of Adrianople on 9 August 378?
options: Goths destroyed an eastern army and killed its emperor
Alaric was defeated by a half-Vandal general
The Goths captured Constantinople for a week
The Huns drove the Goths across the Danube
Romans crushed the Gothic rebels and expelled them
questions.explanation: At Adrianople, in modern European Turkey, the rebel Goths wiped out an eastern army and killed its emperor. Afterwards Rome had to settle them as allies.
questions.sourceQuote: At Adrianople, in modern European Turkey, on 9 August 378 they destroyed an eastern army and killed its emperor.

questions.question: Which notable person did the Goths carry off as a hostage when they sacked Rome in 410?
options: The commander of the city guard
The emperor's own sister
The emperor's young son
The bishop of Rome
The leader of the Senate
questions.explanation: The emperor's sister was taken as a hostage. Citizens were also tortured to reveal hidden valuables.
questions.sourceQuote: Citizens were tortured to reveal hidden valuables, and the emperor's own sister was carried off as a hostage.
